Do you feel dizzy or have double vision when trying to move?
Is there any numbness or tingling in your lower limbs?
Has this difficulty with walking developed gradually over weeks/months?
Are you taking any medications for mental health or nausea?
Do you notice any trembling or shaking of your hands, especially at rest?
Has your thinking or memory become slower recently?
Have you had any trouble controlling your bladder?
Is your voice becoming softer or quieter?

Large volume lumbar puncture (therapeutic tap - drain 30-50ml CSF) to assess gait improvement

dx_raw:
ASK:
1. After the lumbar puncture, did your walking improve at all?
2. Are there any frontal release signs present (grasp reflex, palmomental reflex, glabellar tap)?
3. Was the Evans index (ratio of frontal horn width to brain width) measured on the MRI - is it greater than 0.3?
4. Do you have any difficulty with initiating movement or turning?

DIAGNOSIS: Normal pressure hydrocephalus - gait apraxia/predominant gait disturbance variant with normal ventricular size on imaging, suggesting possible NPH with atypical/imaging-negative presentation, or alternatively idiopathic gait apraxia of the elderly
